parts.note: a bunch of this tropical fruit is called a hand, so it is literally picked off in hands rather than one at a time

explanation.surface: A remark about fruit gathered manually rather than by machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests hand-picking at harvest; the trick is that the clusters of this fruit on the stalk are themselves called hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A long yellow tropical fruit that grows in clusters known as hands.

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is the usual graduate's degree
sic is Latin for 'so' or 'thus', printed to show a quotation is exact

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a university graduate is surprisingly naive.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain and elementary, with no refinement, is a synonym of unsophisticated.

clue.text: Time for tea? And French no different

indicators.note: the word posh is placed in the word for a deed, the clue's 'indeed' split into two words

parts.note: a deed is an action
U stands for upper-class, a British label for posh speech and manners

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a certain form of the card game bridge is very upmarket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' must be read as 'in deed': U (posh) goes in ACTION (deed). Auction bridge is the older form of the card game, before contract bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Auction bridge is a variety of the card game in which players bid for the right to name trumps.

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters of these words are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters I, T and S, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs that the thing is blended with bargain-bin scented petals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potpourri' suggests dried petals, but here it means a medley. 'mixed' rearranges ITSCHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A medley imitating or combining several styles is a pastiche, much as a musical potpourri strings tunes together.

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the following words are put together in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone who has spent far too much finds themselves in an awkward spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges the fifteen letters of OVERSPENT and TRICKY; the whole clue also describes the state of having run out of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being destitute after spending too much is exactly a penniless, needy plight.

clue.text: Strategies found playing chess with me

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved about like pieces in a game, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone discovers tactics by playing a game of chess with the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans or plots devised to reach a goal are strategies.

clue.text: Revolutionary air spray may be bought here

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary, is a crossword stalwart for CHE
a fine spray of droplets in the air is a mist

explanation.surface: A rebellious aerosol is said to be on sale at this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like an adjective for the spray but is the noun Che. A British chemist is a pharmacy, a shop also selling toiletries such as sprays.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a pharmacy or drugstore is called a chemist, a shop where such items are sold.

clue.text: Displaying text about dog — the show-off

indicators.note: about means the letters of the anagram go around the dog's name
displaying here means laying out afresh, so the letters of the next word are arranged anew

parts.note: Rover is the stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: Someone showing off a message about their pet dog is a show-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Displaying' rearranges TEXT into EXTT, and 'about' puts ROVER inside it, after EXT.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, attention-loving person, the opposite of an introvert, is a typical show-off.

explanation.surface: A question whether interference never lets up.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant means unchanging, as in a fixed state; interference means crackling noise on a radio or television signal.

indicators.note: kept in means one word is held inside another

parts.note: to vet is to check or examine
hunks are muscular men, he-men

explanation.surface: An ardent observation that the muscular men were held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing intense, forceful feeling is a synonym of passionate.

clue.text: Page company saying you are on line

indicators.note: saying means we take the sound of the words rather than their spelling

parts.note: spoken quickly, 'you are' sounds like the two letters U and R
a tier is a row or line, as of seats

explanation.surface: A firm's page reads like a text message on a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Page' looks like a sheet of paper but is a court attendant; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is a youthful attendant at court, and a courtier is any attendant at a royal court.

clue.text: Man exercising discipline in clinical operation, initially

definitions.text: Man exercising discipline in clinical operation, initially

indicators.note: initially means we take the opening letter of each word in the clue

explanation.surface: A man showing control during a hospital procedure at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of the six preceding words; the whole clue also describes a doctor at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Medico is informal slang for a doctor, a man practising medicine.

clue.text: He may be needed for just in case!

definitions.text: He may be needed for just in case!

parts.words: He may be needed for just in case!
parts.note: 'just in case' reads as a precaution, but means a fair outcome in a legal case, where a lawyer would be required

explanation.surface: Someone advises keeping a person on hand as a precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just in case' looks like a precaution; read 'just' as fair and 'case' as a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer, especially in the US, who represents clients in court cases.

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about means the gushing word is wrapped around the letter for independent

parts.note: to gush is to spout, as a fountain does

explanation.surface: A miserable independent politician's piece poured out.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling severe mental distress makes one wretched.

parts.note: a sort is a person, as in 'a good sort'
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone who is rude and objectionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective meaning rude, but is the noun: a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie is a sally or attack by troops, a military offensive.

indicators.note: about means the word for balance surrounds the word for exercise

parts.note: the balance is the rest, what remains
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Advice to work on poise around a teetotal lifestyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balance' means remainder here, not poise.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderation and self-control, keeping oneself in check, amount to sobriety.

indicators.note: middle points to the central letter of the following word

parts.note: rants are tirades

explanation.surface: Benefits for people in middle age make them angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle age' looks like a stage of life, but means the middle letter of AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sums of money awarded, such as student funding, are allowances.

clue.text: Say, I'm in favour of a jar

indicators.note: say means we hear the words spoken rather than read their spelling

parts.note: this phrase becomes '(I) am for a', which spoken sounds like the vessel

explanation.surface: Someone declares they approve of a certain pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm in favour of a' becomes '(I) am for a', and 'Say' says it aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall two-handled ancient Greek or Roman vessel for wine or oil is a kind of jar.

clue.text: The sort that is in glasses?

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation goes inside the word for glasses

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles, glasses
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of thing lives in a drinking glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glasses' suggests drinking vessels but means spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: A biological species is a kind or type of creature.

indicators.note: round means the word for shipment goes around the motorway letter

parts.note: transit is the conveying of goods, shipment
M is the label for a British motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Send a consignment around the ring road.
explanation.definitionFit: To send out or pass on, as a signal or message, is to dispatch.

parts.note: an oil painting is a work of art
the suffix -less means without, having no

explanation.surface: Someone says Frank is not good-looking, a British idiom for being plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no oil painting' is a British idiom for plain-looking; 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective, and 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open and without guile, as candid speech is, means artless.

clue.text: One politician very big on European force

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
OS is the clothing size outsize

explanation.surface: A single, oversized legislator leaning on Europe's military.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' looks like a noun but is the verb; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose is to compel acceptance of something, to force it on others.

clue.text: At home, diplomacy surrounding queen's consort

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for diplomacy is placed around the queen's letters

parts.note: tact is diplomacy
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher for the Queen

explanation.surface: A tactful palace setting around the Queen's husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consort' looks like the royal spouse but is the verb, to associate.
explanation.definitionFit: To consort with people is to mix and associate with them.

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ease is calm composure

explanation.surface: Mock the calm self-possession of the Conservative Party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock or make fun of someone is to deride them.

indicators.note: first means the gangster comes ahead of the flash in the answer

parts.note: a hood, short for hoodlum, is a gangster
a wink is a flash or instant

explanation.surface: A showy mobster betrays someone before anyone else does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flash' reads as showy but means an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive or trick someone is to double-cross them.

clue.text: It may have obscure meaning having no point

definitions.text: It may have obscure meaning having no point

indicators.note: obscure means the letters of the word are confused or muddled

parts.note: N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Something whose sense is murky and pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' rearranges MEANING less N ('having no point'); the clue as a whole describes a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle or mystery whose sense is hidden is an enigma.

clue.text: Stop playing piano with sad arrangement

indicators.note: playing means the letters perform a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Quit playing the keyboard with a sorrowful tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a command but is the noun: a main organ stop. 'with ... arrangement' completes the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The diapason is a principal organ stop giving the instrument's basic tone.

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat means posed
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A send-up that posed with fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire uses ridicule and exaggeration to mock, as parody does.
